content:
According to the Financial Times, the latest court documents show that OpenAI is disappointed with the adoption of ChatGPT through Apple Intelligence, stating that the feature has "performed far below expectations" since its launch in 2024. Details below.

OpenAI is asking the court to rule before trial

In August 2025, Elon Musk said that X, now under SpaceXAI, would sue Apple and OpenAI over allegations of conspiring to suppress competitors. The dispute stemmed from OpenAI's deal with Apple to integrate ChatGPT into Apple Intelligence and Siri.

After the case was formally filed, the litigation actually went beyond Musk's original public complaint about App Store rankings. X and SpaceXAI also accused Apple of trying to hinder the development of "super apps," including X's effort to transform itself into an "everything app."

In the weeks and months that followed, the involved companies submitted briefs, allegations, and defences to the court. Apple and OpenAI have consistently argued that the agreement is not an exclusive partnership as the lawsuit claims; court documents have also revealed new details about how the collaboration operates behind the scenes.

One of those details surfaced in a filing submitted by OpenAI today. As first reported by the Financial Times, OpenAI "said it was disappointed that Apple failed to generate much interest among iPhone users after striking a deal in 2024 to bring a ChatGPT-powered 'Apple Intelligence' to the devices."

Quoting the report:

Wednesday's court documents indicate that when the 2024 deal was struck, OpenAI expected to generate a "halo effect" from Apple's promotion and brand association, and to attract more subscriptions from Apple Intelligence users. However, one month after the ChatGPT integration launched, progress "appeared to get off to a slow start," and OpenAI accordingly lowered its forecast for weekly active user growth. The documents also state that by summer 2025, "the performance of Apple's ChatGPT integration was clearly below expectations."

The report notes that today's filing contains several redacted exchanges, but the unredacted portions show that OpenAI executives were concerned Apple might "want to move faster" and seek out a different AI partner.

When Apple Intelligence was first announced in 2024, Craig Federighi said in an interview that Apple ultimately wanted to let users choose from different AI models, specifically mentioning Google Gemini as a potential future integration partner.

That particular partnership ultimately did not materialise, but Apple later adopted Google's Gemini model to partially power the next-generation Siri AI, and Xcode has also expanded support for coding agents from Anthropic, Google, and OpenAI.

Popular comment from OliveCocktail

As others have said, when I want to use ChatGPT, I go straight to their standalone app. In fact, that's my preferred way, because I don't want all my voice commands mixed together. I prefer letting Apple handle my personalised, contextually relevant information. I've never been clear on the privacy implications of using the ChatGPT "integration," and I can't even be bothered to look into it, because I know I won't use it. By contrast, I'm comfortable with the privacy aspects of using Apple Intelligence/Siri.

Returning to today's filing, the Financial Times points out that the documents also flag the way Apple implemented the ChatGPT integration as one possible reason for low adoption, because the feature is off by default.

Finally, OpenAI is also, as Reuters reports, pointing to SpaceX's recent securities filings as evidence that undermines SpaceXAI's claim that the Apple partnership harms competition. In its filing, OpenAI states that SpaceX's IPO registration statement is full of disclosures that are "directly contrary to the competitive harm alleged in the lawsuit."

On these grounds, OpenAI is asking Judge Mark Pittman to rule in its favour on SpaceXAI's antitrust claims before trial. The case is currently scheduled to go to trial in January.
